subject: [PATCH 13/22] mm/hugetlb: restrict pool growth to common memory

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch restricts the growth of HugeTLB pools to nodes that have common memory, preventing allocations on nodes without this capability. The change is made by modifying various functions in the mm/hugetlb.c file to use N_MEMORY_COMMON instead of N_MEMORY for allocating and growing hugepage pools. This restriction can be loosened later if needed. Currently, all memory is considered common, so the behavior remains unchanged.

reviews.author: Richard Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng noted that the new code may lead to an uneven or smaller pool size due to delayed node allocation, and suggested moving the nodes_and() call inside the loop to restore the original behavior.
reviews.raw_body:
For a global request the caller passes &node_states[N_MEMORY], so before this patch
the grow loop read the live mask on every alloc_pool_huge_folio().
Now the mask is sampled once, before the loop.

The loop drops hugetlb_lock and can run for a long time. If a node gets its first
memoroy in that window, the old code would start using it. The new code won't, until
the next write to nr_hugepages.

So the pool can end up uneven, or smaller than requested if the other nodes are full.

I think the nodes_and() should be placed inside the loop to keep the old behavior ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a potential issue with hugepage distribution when there's a race between hugetlb allocation and memory hotplug, but downplayed its significance as an 'innocuous corner case'. They agreed to retain the old behavior if it's reliable.
reviews.raw_body:
I can make the adjustment, but the concern is that previously we'd
start spreading the distribution of hugepages differently when there's a
race between hugetlb allocation and memory hotplug?

That seems like a pretty innocuous corner case to be worried about.

I can see about retaining the old behavior, but i'm not sure what you're
describing is reliable behavior already.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch restricts the growth of HugeTLB pools to nodes that have common memory (N_MEMORY_COMMON). It achieves this by changing the allocation mask in several functions, ensuring that new pool folios are only allocated on these nodes. This change will cause hugepage allocations to fail on nodes without N_MEMORY_COMMON. The original allowed mask for pool shrinking and demotion is preserved to allow existing pool folios to still be found on any online-memory node.
